title: Interband plasmons due to Mexican hat dispersion in two-dimensional materials with inverted bands
abstract: Two-dimensional topological materials with Mexican-hat dispersion exhibit numerous nontrivial features, such as double-valued isoenergetic contours in k-space, strong mixing of electron and hole states, a van Hove singularity in the density of states, and specific quantum geometric properties. We find that, due to these features, Mexican-hat dispersion significantly strengthens interband plasmons, reduces their damping, and gives rise to an additional branch of the plasmon spectrum when electron-hole symmetry is broken. The plasmon spectra are limited to a finite range of the wave vector, the boundaries of which depend on the strength of the electron-electron interaction. We also reveal a relationship between the features of the plasmon spectrum and singularities of the joint density of states with a finite plasmon wave vector q, as well as features of the interband quantum metric, which also depend on q.
summary: This theoretical study examines interband plasmons in 2D topological materials exhibiting Mexican-hat dispersion. The authors show that this unique band structure significantly enhances plasmon strength and predicts an additional low-frequency plasmon branch when electron-hole symmetry is broken. The results highlight the deep connection between plasmon excitation modes and singularities in the joint density of states.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the unique electronic structure arising from Mexican-hat dispersion (MHD) in 2D topological materials affects the properties of interband plasmons (IBPs).
main_result: MHD significantly strengthens the plasmons, reduces their damping, and causes the emergence of an additional, low-frequency plasmon branch when electron-hole symmetry is broken.
method: The analysis is performed using the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) framework, focusing on calculating the polarization function, the joint density of states (JDOS), and the interband overlap function.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D topological material with inverted bands, modeled using the BHZ Hamiltonian. Key features include double-valued isoenergetic contours and a Van Hove singularity.
key_observables: Interband plasmon spectrum ($\omega_p(q)$), Joint Density of States ($	ext{JDOS}_q$), and the interband quantum metric.
important_parameters: The hybridization parameter $a$, the e-h asymmetry parameter $d$, and the plasmon wave vector $q$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes spatial inversion symmetry and treats spin as a good quantum number; the low-frequency branch analysis is restricted to cases where e-h symmetry is broken.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MHD dispersion in both symmetric and asymmetric cases, and show the calculated plasmon spectra ($\omega_{p1}, \omega_{p2}$) relative to the saddle-point singularity energies ($w_{s1}, w_{s2}$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by detailing the general formalism (Hamiltonian, overlap function, JDOS), analyzing the plasmon spectrum in the e-h symmetric case, and finally addressing the effects and emergence of the additional low-frequency branch when e-h symmetry is broken.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between electronic band structure singularities (like Van Hove points) and collective excitations (plasmons) is a core topic in condensed matter theory, relevant for understanding plasmonic responses in novel 2D materials.
